verdict.rationale: Thoropass's official MCP server lets an assistant act in the workspace 'within limits you set', and the setup docs say to add or remove certain items 'depending on what you want your agent to be able to do', which suggests first-party scoping of agent permissions. The evidence is thin, though: it never describes issuing dedicated API credentials or tokens, what the scopes are, or how they are enforced. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of agent-specific credential or token issuance, a defined scope/permission model, read-only vs write separation, credential revocation/rotation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
